content:
Been sketching out a path toward eventually formalizing the hydrogen atom's energy spectrum and wanted to share the idea before going further with it.

The natural route is the analytic one, unbounded operators, spectral theory, all the machinery needed to make the Coulomb Hamiltonian rigorous.

There's an algebraic story too: the hydrogen atom has a certain symmetry and if you lean on the representation theory hard enough, the energy levels and their degeneracies just fall out of group theory, almost without touching an actual Hamiltonian. I'm trying to build that route instead, get the algebra fully worked out first and only afterward come back and show that the real, concrete operators satisfy whatever the algebra needed all along.

So the project ends up split naturally into a math half and a physics half, developed somewhat independently, that need to be stitched together at the end.

If this is interesting to you, the repo's here: https://github.com/TomOleDiem/QuantumRepresentationTheory, and the blueprint (roadmap of theorems and how they connect) is here: https://tomolediem.github.io/QuantumRepresentationTheory/blueprint/

Genuinely happy for people to poke holes in it and point out mistakes.
Hi Tom! Nice to meet you! ccing @Gregory Loges here who has done some work in this direction.

Hi Joseph, great work you are doing here.
I couldnt find any messages on zulip or commits from Gregory,
could you point me towards some of them?

Hi Tom - thanks for reaching out, and welcome!
I did some work with LRL calculations earlier this year when I was learning Lean (e.g. see physlib#1026). This was with a regularized Hamiltonian and Schwartz maps since at that time the unbounded operators / spectral theory was absent from Physlib - it would be great to get these results "upgraded" to the proper singular potential and fully fleshed out.

I had a quick look at your blueprint and it looks good! At this point my only comment is that I think we should avoid angular momentum vectors since this is a quirk of 3d and really the correct object is an antisymmetric 2-tensor.
Happy to chat more about the line of attack :slight_smile: I am largely preoccupied through August but have been trying to pop in here every few days to check in.

Quick update: Been proving a lot more since I last posted here. Rather than just going after hydrogen directly, I've been trying to prove things at the general level and then apply them to both hydrogen and the harmonic oscillator, in any spatial dimension. Here's the new blueprint:
https://tomolediem.github.io/QuantumRepresentationTheory/blueprint/dep_graph_document.html.
To be upfront about it though, several of the big theorems are still just admitted or plain sorry on my end, like the general highest-weight/Weyl-character machinery and a handful of analytic facts are still open.
Going through it maybe there are already a few things Physlib worthy.
Im still unsure how to best integrate as im still figuring out what the correct abstraction to the problem is.
Always happy for comments and feedback!
